answer: Require each identity to prove it held a unique dataset continuously over time, a proof-of-space-time where the storage must be present at random audits. A karst cave is hollowed over ages, not overnight, and at its zenith the proof is simple: the data is either there or it is not. A terrace of rented disks, present for one audit and gone the next, is caught at the second check, because the data must be there at every moment. One disk serves only one identity's proof.
